A King-plot comparison with the \({}^{1}S_{0}\rightarrow{}^{1}P_{1}\) transition at \(214~\mathrm{nm}\) gives field- and mass-shift parameters of \(F_{307.6,214}=1.17(5)\) and \(K=-153(60)~\mathrm{GHz\,u}\). These results provide the spectroscopic basis for narrow-line cooling and precision measurements based on zinc, including the development of an optical clock.

AI.tldr: Laser-induced fluorescence spectroscopy of the Zn intercombination transition at 307.6 nm yields kHz-level isotope shifts, hyperfine constants for ⁶⁷Zn, and King-plot parameters, providing a foundation for narrow-line cooling and optical clocks.
AI.motivation: To improve precision of isotope shift measurements for Zn by two orders of magnitude and resolve hyperfine structure for ⁶⁷Zn, enabling narrow-line cooling and optical clock development.
AI.method: Laser-induced fluorescence spectroscopy of the ¹S₀→³P₁ intercombination transition at 307.6 nm; King-plot comparison with the ¹S₀→¹P₁ transition at 214 nm.
AI.result: kHz-level isotope shifts for all stable Zn isotopes; for ⁶⁷Zn: δν_COG⁶⁷,⁶⁴=1085.933(4) MHz, A=608.922(1) MHz, B=-18.995(4) MHz; King-plot parameters F=1.17(5), K=-153(60) GHz·u.
AI.conclusion: Provides spectroscopic foundation for narrow-line cooling and precision measurements in Zn, including optical clock development.

title: Sustainable Metal-Organic Framework Water Harvesters in the Artificial Intelligence Era
comment: 10 pages of main text, 26 total pages. 3 Figures and 1 Table of Content Graphic
summary: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are excellent candidates for water harvesting due to their tunable pore environments, which can be precisely engineered to capture and release water in arid conditions. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into MOF discovery can further accelerate the design of high-performance sorbents by identifying structural features that enhance atmospheric water harvesting (AWH), stability, and cycling efficiency. In this Perspective, we examine key MOF design principles, including cooperative adsorption, operational relative humidity (RH), uptake capacity, hysteresis, and scalability. We highlight recent design advancements such as multivariate strategies and long-arm linker extension, and examine how these principles tune pore capacity and hydrophilicity, while preserving stability and crystallinity. Furthermore, we discuss how AI, large language models (LLMs), and data mining can accelerate the discovery process through predictive synthesis, inverse design, and elucidating synthesis-structure-property relationships for the next generation of MOF water harvesters.

AI.tldr: This Perspective examines MOF design principles for atmospheric water harvesting and discusses how AI, LLMs, and data mining can accelerate the discovery of next-generation MOF sorbents by predicting synthesis, enabling inverse design, and elucidating structure-property relationships.
AI.motivation: To accelerate the discovery of high-performance MOF sorbents for atmospheric water harvesting by integrating AI methods with established design principles, addressing the need for efficient water capture in arid conditions.
AI.method: The paper reviews key MOF design principles (cooperative adsorption, RH control, uptake capacity, hysteresis, scalability) and emerging strategies (multivariate synthesis, long-arm linker extension). It proposes integrating AI, LLMs, and data mining for predictive synthesis, inverse design, and synthesis-structure-property relationship elucidation.
AI.result: Identification of tunable pore environments and design strategies that balance pore capacity, hydrophilicity, stability, and crystallinity. The framework shows how AI can systematically accelerate MOF discovery for water harvesting.
AI.conclusion: Combining MOF design principles with AI-driven approaches offers a promising pathway to discover next-generation water harvesting sorbents with enhanced performance and cycling efficiency.

title: Controlled Loop Expansion for Strained Twisted Bilayer Graphene
summary: We develop a controlled diagrammatic framework for periodic Anderson models,and apply it to heterostrained magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG) at charge neutrality using the topological heavy-fermion formulation. Building on arXiv:2604.14278, we organize self-energy insertions and perform a Dyson resummation to any order in the small parameter $s^2$ -- the fraction of the moiré Brillouin zone with nontrivial quantum geometry. For strained MATBG, the expansion remains controlled down to arbitrarily low temperatures as long as the strain induced energy scale is not too small. In the flat-chiral limit, an emergent approximate $\rm{U}(1)$ symmetry forbids the leading scattering channel and leaves the Mott bands sharp at order $s^2$. This is in stark contrast to the unstrained case, where the linewidth is of order $N_f s^2 U$ with $U$ the on-site $f$-$f$ Hubbard interaction and $N_f$ the number of $f$ states per site. Away from the chiral limit, the linewidth is non-zero at order $s^2$ but more than an order of magnitude smaller than in the unstrained case. The strain-induced energy scale also imprints itself directly on the spectrum: as an electron-phonon-like kink in the dispersion, and as an additional flat ``trion'' band -- a single-particle excitation bound to a local $f$ particle-hole pair. We use the framework to predict the Quantum Twisting Microscope spectrum at one-loop order for both strained and unstrained MATBG, and compare with recent experiments.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a controlled diagrammatic framework for periodic Anderson models, applies it to strained MATBG at charge neutrality, and shows that strain suppresses quasiparticle linewidths, introduces electron-phonon-like kinks and trion bands, and enables controlled expansion down to low temperatures.
AI.motivation: To develop a controlled theoretical framework for strongly correlated moiré systems, specifically to understand how strain modifies the electronic properties of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG), which has been shown in arXiv:2604.14278 to be described by a topological heavy-fermion model.
AI.method: A controlled diagrammatic framework for periodic Anderson models is developed, organizing self-energy insertions with Dyson resummation to any order in the small parameter s² (fraction of moiré Brillouin zone with nontrivial quantum geometry). Applied to heterostrained MATBG using the topological heavy-fermion formulation.
AI.result: For strained MATBG, the expansion is controlled down to arbitrarily low temperatures provided strain energy scale is not too small. In the flat-chiral limit, emergent U(1) symmetry forbids leading scattering, keeping Mott bands sharp at order s² — contrasting with unstrained case where linewidth scales as N_f s² U. Away from chiral limit, linewidth is nonzero at order s² but >10× smaller than unstrained. Strain imprints as electron-phonon-like kinks and a flat "trion" band (single-particle excitation bound to local f particle-hole pair).
AI.conclusion: The framework provides predictive power for Quantum Twisting Microscope spectra at one-loop order for both strained and unstrained MATBG, enabling direct comparison with recent experiments.

title: Induced nonlinear phase shift of forward volume spin waves in magnetic films and one-dimensional magnonic crystals
summary: A differential phase shift of a low-power spin wave (SW) induced by a high-power pumping wave co-propagating at different frequencies in perpendicularly magnetized magnetic films has been studied. We find that this effect for forward volume SWs propagating in yttrium iron garnet (YIG) films is stronger than that for surface SWs propagating in tangentially magnetized films. The results show that the induced nonlinear phase shift up to 180° takes place for pumping wave power of a few milliwatts. The phenomenon paves the way for fast and energy-efficient control of one-dimensional magnon transport.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the differential phase shift of a low-power spin wave induced by a high-power pumping wave co-propagating at different frequencies in perpendicularly magnetized magnetic films, specifically forward volume SWs in YIG films. The effect is stronger than for surface SWs and achieves a nonlinear phase shift up to 180° with only a few milliwatts of pumping power, enabling energy-efficient control of magnon transport.
AI.motivation: To achieve fast and energy-efficient control of one-dimensional magnon transport by exploiting nonlinear phase shifts induced by a co-propagating high-power pumping wave.
AI.method: Experimental study of differential phase shift induced by a high-power pumping wave co-propagating at different frequencies with a low-power spin wave in perpendicularly magnetized magnetic films (forward volume SWs in YIG), compared with surface SWs in tangentially magnetized films.
AI.result: The nonlinear phase shift effect is stronger for forward volume SWs in perpendicularly magnetized YIG films than for surface SWs in tangentially magnetized films. A phase shift up to 180° is achieved with pumping power of only a few milliwatts.
AI.conclusion: This nonlinear phase shift phenomenon enables fast and energy-efficient control of one-dimensional magnon transport.

title: Estimates of ground state energies for the quantum SK and 2D-EA model, using deGennes-Suzuki-Kubo mean-field annealing dynamics
summary: We perform a large scale simulation of quantum annealing in the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) spin glass up to a system size $N=40000$ to estimate its ground state energy using the deGennes-Suzuki-Kubo mean-field Ising dynamics, extending the earlier results (reported in Eur. Phys. J. B {\bf 98}, 226 (2025)). Here we numerically solve the deGennes-Suzuki-Kubo annealing dynamics to obtain the spin configurations and subsequently the ground state energy for a given system size at the end of the annealing (to the desired quantum system at the corresponding values of the transverse field), starting from a quantum paramagnetic state. The method shows high efficiency, with an overall algorithmic cost of $O(N^3)$ in estimating the energy of the ground state. We later extend this method to study the ground state energy of the Edwards-Anderson (EA) spin glass on a square lattice.

AI.tldr: Large-scale simulation of quantum annealing in SK spin glass (up to N=40,000) using deGennes-Suzuki-Kubo mean-field Ising dynamics, achieving O(N³) cost for ground state energy estimation, with extension to EA spin glass on square lattice.
AI.motivation: To estimate the ground state energy of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick spin glass at large system sizes (N=40,000) by extending previous mean-field annealing dynamics results, and to extend the method to Edwards-Anderson spin glasses on square lattices.
AI.method: Numerically solves the deGennes-Suzuki-Kubo mean-field Ising dynamics for quantum annealing, starting from a quantum paramagnetic state. Spin configurations and ground state energy are obtained at the end of annealing for desired transverse field values. The method has overall algorithmic cost O(N³).
AI.result: Demonstrates high efficiency with O(N³) cost for ground state energy estimation in SK spin glass up to N=40,000; method is also extended to EA spin glass on a square lattice.
AI.conclusion: The deGennes-Suzuki-Kubo mean-field dynamics provides an efficient O(N³) approach for estimating ground state energies in both SK and EA spin glass models via quantum annealing simulation.

title: On certain combinatorial expressions of TASEP transition probabilities
summary:
We study combinatorial structures arising from finite-time transition probabilities of the Totally Asymmetric Simple Exclusion Process with open boundary conditions. While much of the existing combinatorial theory regarding the TASEP concerns the steady-state distribution, we focus instead on the transient dynamics. We first show that the enumeration of transition sequences between two configurations of the open TASEP is equivalent to the enumeration of standard Young tableaux of a family of non-classical shapes which have been of recent interest in the combinatorial literature. This extends to the open-boundary setting the correspondence between the TASEP with periodic boundaries and cylindric tableaux.
  We then introduce a family of tableau-like objects associated with Young diagrams in which repetitions of cells are allowed, subject to the partial order induced by the diagram. For each diagram, we collect the numbers of these objects into an exponential generating function. We prove that the entries of the homogeneous open TASEP transition matrix can be expressed as signed sums of such generating functions over suitable families of diagrams. This gives a combinatorial and order-theoretic interpretation of finite-time transition probabilities for the open TASEP, analogous to the combinatorial mappings known for steady-state probabilities.

AI.tldr: This paper studies transient dynamics of the open TASEP, showing that transition sequence enumeration corresponds to standard Young tableaux of non-classical shapes, and introduces a new family of tableau-like objects whose generating functions express finite-time transition probabilities via signed sums.
AI.motivation: To extend the combinatorial understanding of the TASEP from steady-state distributions to transient (finite-time) dynamics, particularly for open boundary conditions which lack the cylindrical symmetry exploited in periodic cases.
AI.method: The authors establish a bijection between open TASEP transition sequences and standard Young tableaux of non-classical shapes, and introduce a new combinatorial object (tableau-like with repeated cells) whose exponential generating functions yield signed-sum expressions for homogeneous open TASEP transition matrix entries.
AI.result: Transition sequence enumeration for open TASEP equals SYT enumeration of non-classical shapes; finite-time transition probabilities are expressed as signed sums of exponential generating functions of the new tableau-like objects over families of Young diagrams.
AI.conclusion: This provides a combinatorial and order-theoretic interpretation of finite-time open TASEP transition probabilities, analogous to existing combinatorial mappings for steady-state probabilities, and extends the periodic-boundary/cylindric-tableaux correspondence to the open-boundary setting.

title: Hole-doped superconductivity above 100 K in infinite-layer cuprate thin films
summary: Since the discovery of superconductivity in (La,Ba)2CuO2 (Ref.~\cite{bednorz1986possible}), a broad family of structurally distinct cuprate superconductors has been proposed or engineered to elucidate the physics of high-temperature superconductivity~\cite{chu2015hole,plakida2010high}. Among them, the infinite-layer cuprate has the simplest structure, consisting only of the essential ingredients for superconductivity: CuO$_2$ square planes separated by spacer ions~\cite{siegrist1988parent}. Despite being proposed nearly 40 years ago, the hole-doped superconductivity via chemical substitution in this compound has not yet been achieved, a fundamental open question in the field. Here, we report the observation of superconductivity in the hole-doped infinite-layer cuprate thin film. Measurements of resistivity and magnetic-field response in Sr1-xRbxCuO2 single-crystal thin films show superconducting transitions with a high onset temperature of 100 K. Hole doping is achieved via the synergistic effect of rubidium substitution and apical oxygen incorporation, as evidenced by structural analysis and transport measurements. As the parent structure of the cuprate family~\cite{chu2015hole}, hole-doped infinite-layer cuprate provides a unique platform for revisiting key puzzles in cuprate superconductors~\cite{keimer2015quantum,tsuei2000pairing,armitage2010progress,dagotto1994correlated}, including strange metal~\cite{proust2019remarkable,taillefer2010scattering} and electron-hole symmetry~\cite{tohyama2004asymmetry,segawa2010zero,lee2014asymmetry}, while bridging to cuprate-nickelate symmetry~\cite{li2019superconductivity,zeng2022superconductivity,chow2025bulk,lechermann2020late}.

AI.tldr: The paper reports the first successful observation of hole-doped superconductivity in infinite-layer cuprate (Sr₁₋ₓRbₓCuO₂) thin films, achieving a superconducting onset temperature of 100 K via rubidium substitution and apical oxygen incorporation, thus resolving a 40-year-old open question.
AI.motivation: Despite nearly 40 years since the discovery of cuprate superconductors, hole-doped superconductivity via chemical substitution in the simplest infinite-layer cuprate structure had not been achieved, leaving a fundamental open question in the field.
AI.method: Hole doping was achieved through a synergistic effect of rubidium (Rb) substitution (creating Sr₁₋ₓRbₓCuO₂) and apical oxygen incorporation in single-crystal thin films, characterized by resistivity and magnetic-field response measurements along with structural analysis and transport measurements.
AI.result: Superconducting transitions with a high onset temperature of 100 K were observed in Sr₁₋ₓRbₓCuO₂ single-crystal thin films via resistivity and magnetic-field response measurements.
AI.conclusion: Realizing hole-doped infinite-layer cuprate provides a unique minimal platform for revisiting key puzzles in cuprate superconductors such as strange metal behavior and electron-hole asymmetry, while also bridging to cuprate-nickelate symmetry studies.

title: Critical states and anomalous wave transport in an aperiodic polariton monotile
summary: Recently "the Hat" monotile was introduced into the family of aperiodic tilings and quasicrystals boasting physical properties lying at the boundary of ordered and disordered systems. Here we study the two-dimensional wave transport, transverse localization and scaling properties of the quantum modes in a Monotile quasilattice. Our system is based on reconfigurable optical lattices for cavity-polaritons which provide flexible means to study wavepacket dynamics, strong nonlinear phenomena, and power-driven condensation in this new type of an aperiodic tiling. We confirm the existence of localized and critical states in the Monotile through direct diagonalization of the Schrödinger equation. Scaling analysis on the moments of the wavefunction distribution reveals anomalous transport regimes of super-diffusive and near sub-diffusive polariton transport associated with the fractal structure of the Monotile Hilbert space. We propose a strategy using resonantly excited polariton fluids to verify our findings.

AI.tldr: This paper studies wave transport, localization, and scaling properties of quantum modes in a Monotile (Hat) quasilattice using cavity-polariton optical lattices, confirming localized and critical states with anomalous transport regimes, and proposes experimental verification via polariton fluids.
AI.motivation: To investigate the wave transport properties and quantum mode localization in the newly discovered "Hat" monotile aperiodic tiling, bridging the gap between ordered and disordered systems.
AI.method: Direct diagonalization of the Schrödinger equation for the Monotile quasilattice, scaling analysis of wavefunction moment distributions, and a proposed strategy using resonantly excited polariton fluids in reconfigurable optical lattices.
AI.result: Confirmed existence of localized and critical states; scaling analysis reveals anomalous transport regimes including super-diffusive and near sub-diffusive polariton transport linked to the fractal Hilbert space structure of the Monotile.
AI.conclusion: The Monotile quasilattice exhibits rich transport behavior (super-diffusive to near sub-diffusive) with localized and critical quantum states, and the proposed polariton fluid platform offers a feasible experimental route to verify these predictions.

title: Restoring Velocity Immunity via Dynamic Mirror Compensation in a Large-Area Dual-Atom-Interferometer Gyroscope
summary: We propose and demonstrate a dynamical mirror compensation scheme to restore velocity immunity in a large-area dual-atom-interferometer gyroscope. In an ideal Mach-Zehnder configuration, the phase shift is inherently immune to atomic velocity, but this property is broken by the Earth's rotation via the Coriolis effect. We overcome this by actively rotating the Raman mirrors during the pulse sequence to cancel the time-dependent angular offset. The implementation relies on a decouplable calibration-compensation chain to remove rotation-induced time-dependent terms. The scheme is validated on a dual-atom-interferometer gyroscope with an interference area of 21.1 cm^2. After compensation, the phase's dependence on atomic velocity is reduced 40-fold, and the velocity contribution to scale-factor stability is evaluated to be 0.13 ppm. The sensor achieves a rotation sensitivity of 1.3\times10^{-8} rad/s/Hz^{1/2} and a stability of 1.9\times10^{-10} rad/s at 4500 s integration, together with a common-mode noise rejection ratio of up to 459, demonstrated in a seismic event. This work removes a key obstacle to scale-factor stabilization in atom-interferometer gyroscopes and paves the way for their applications in inertial navigation and geophysics.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a dynamical mirror compensation scheme to restore velocity immunity in a large-area dual-atom-interferometer gyroscope, achieving a 40-fold reduction in velocity dependence, 0.13 ppm scale-factor stability, and 1.9×10^{-10} rad/s stability at 4500 s.
AI.motivation: The Earth's rotation breaks the inherent velocity immunity of the Mach-Zehnder configuration via the Coriolis effect, degrading scale-factor stability in atom-interferometer gyroscopes and hindering their practical applications in inertial navigation and geophysics.
AI.method: Active rotation of Raman mirrors during the pulse sequence to cancel the time-dependent angular offset, enabled by a decouplable calibration-compensation chain that removes rotation-induced time-dependent terms.
AI.result: 40-fold reduction in phase-velocity dependence; 0.13 ppm velocity contribution to scale-factor stability; rotation sensitivity of 1.3×10^{-8} rad/s/Hz^{1/2}; stability of 1.9×10^{-10} rad/s at 4500 s; common-mode noise rejection ratio up to 459.
AI.conclusion: The work removes a key obstacle to scale-factor stabilization in atom-interferometer gyroscopes and paves the way for their applications in inertial navigation and geophysics.

title: Topological Lifshitz transition-induced bipolarity of anomalous Nernst effect in kagome magnet YCo3
summary: The kagome lattice, renowned for hosting topological band structures and rich magnetic behaviors, offers an exceptional setting to investigate unconventional transport in magnetic topological systems. Controlling the polarity of the anomalous Nernst effect (ANE) is crucial for designing flexible thermoelectric devices, such as thermopiles, where the ability to switch the thermoelectric voltage sign can dramatically enhance energy conversion efficiency and output. Here, we demonstrate such a bipolar ANE in the kagome magnet YCo3, driven by a temperature-induced topological Lifshitz transition. With a Curie temperature TC~225 K, sizable anomalous Hall and Nernst effects emerge below TC. Supported by the first-principles calculations, the AHE and ANE are suggested to be dominated by the intrinsic mechanism. Furthermore, the intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity exhibits a piecewise-linear dependence on magnetization, with an abrupt slope change near 100 K, consistent with the Karplus-Luttinger mechanism. Concurrently, the anomalous Nernst coefficient SAyx reverses its sign around the same temperature, realizing the crucial bipolarity. These anomalies could be interpreted as a topological Lifshitz transition, enabled by the evolution of Co moments that could shift the Fermi level relative to Weyl nodes. Our work reveals YCo3 as a prototypical kagome magnet where temperature and magnetism directly govern both Weyl node topology and the bipolar ANE, opening a pathway to magnetically control thermoelectric output in topological quantum materials.

AI.tldr: This paper demonstrates a bipolar anomalous Nernst effect (ANE) in the kagome magnet YCo₃, driven by a temperature-induced topological Lifshitz transition near 100 K, where the anomalous Nernst coefficient reverses sign, enabling switchable thermoelectric voltage polarity for improved energy conversion.
AI.motivation: Controlling the polarity of the anomalous Nernst effect is crucial for designing flexible thermoelectric devices (e.g., thermopiles), as switching the thermoelectric voltage sign can dramatically enhance energy conversion efficiency and output.
AI.method: Experimental measurements of anomalous Hall effect (AHE) and anomalous Nernst effect (ANE) in YCo₃ (TC ~ 225 K), combined with first-principles calculations to elucidate intrinsic mechanisms and the role of topological Lifshitz transitions.
AI.result: Sizable AHE and ANE emerge below TC; intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity shows piecewise-linear dependence on magnetization with an abrupt slope change near 100 K; the anomalous Nernst coefficient reverses sign at the same temperature, achieving bipolarity.
AI.conclusion: The sign reversal is attributed to a topological Lifshitz transition driven by Co moment evolution, shifting the Fermi level relative to Weyl nodes. YCo₃ is identified as a prototypical kagome magnet where temperature and magnetism govern both Weyl node topology and bipolar ANE, offering a route to magnetically control thermoelectric output in topological quantum materials.

title: Topological superconductivity from Abelian fractional Chern insulators
summary: Can a Laughlin anyon fluid become a topological superconductor? We answer this question for a $ν=1/3$ fractional Chern insulator (FCI) using a $U(3)$ infrared parton theory. Three charge-$e/3$ constituents form the electron, while three constituent pairs form a gauge-invariant charge-$2e$ Cooper pair. The resulting superconductors share an ordinary charge-$2e$ sector but differ in their neutral color response, giving an SC$^\ast$ with the parent Laughlin $U(1)_3$ order, a chiral topological superconductor with $c_-=3/2$, and a strong-pairing anyon superconductor with $c_-=3$. The same framework organizes a nearby $σ_{xy}=0$ charge density wave (CDW) state. At commensurate filling, the normal state and the $c_-=3$ and $c_-=3/2$ superconducting descendants are naturally tied to a period-three density order background, while the SC$^\ast$ branch can preserve microscopic translations. Away from commensuration, a chargon metal can pair into the same $c_-=3/2$ topological superconductor. The FCI, reentrant CDW, and chiral superconductivity are unified in the $U(3)$ parton theory.

AI.tldr: The paper explores whether a ν=1/3 Laughlin anyon fluid (fractional Chern insulator) can transition into a topological superconductor, using a U(3) parton theory. It identifies three superconducting descendants with distinct topological orders (SC* with U(1)_3, chiral topological superconductor with c_-=3/2, and strong-pairing anyon superconductor with c_-=3), and unifies them with charge density wave states in a single theoretical framework.
AI.motivation: To determine if a Laughlin anyon fluid (ν=1/3 fractional Chern insulator) can become a topological superconductor, and to unify the description of nearby competing phases (FCI, CDW, and superconductivity) within a common theoretical framework.
AI.method: A U(3) infrared parton theory where three charge-e/3 constituents form the electron, and three constituent pairs form a gauge-invariant charge-2e Cooper pair. The theory classifies superconducting phases by their neutral color response and ties them to period-three density order backgrounds.
AI.result: Three distinct superconducting descendants exist: SC* (with parent Laughlin U(1)_3 order), a chiral topological superconductor (c_-=3/2), and a strong-pairing anyon superconductor (c_-=3). At commensurate filling, normal state and two SC branches are tied to period-three order; SC* preserves microscopic translations. Away from commensuration, a chargon metal can pair into the c_-=3/2 topological superconductor.
AI.conclusion: The FCI, reentrant CDW, and chiral superconductivity are unified within the U(3) parton theory, establishing a roadmap for realizing topological superconductivity from anyon fluids.

title: Criticality in the disordered $N$-color Ashkin-Teller model
summary: The $N$-color Ashkin-Teller model corresponds to $N$ Ising models coupled by four-spin interactions. We consider the two-dimensional case in presence of quenched disorder and use scale invariant scattering theory to determine all the solutions of the exact renormalization group fixed points equations. The weak disorder sector is characterized by a solution that, for any fixed $N$ larger than 1, is a line of fixed points with Ising thermal exponents and continuously varying magnetic exponents. The number of fixed point solutions allowed by the symmetries of the model increases at strong disorder illustrating the growing dependence on the distributions of the two random couplings. The presence of some critical exponents which do not depend on the symmetry parameter $N$ confirms this type of superuniversality as a peculiar feature of random criticality.

AI.tldr: The paper studies the 2D N-color Ashkin-Teller model with quenched disorder using scale invariant scattering theory. It finds a line of fixed points with Ising thermal exponents and varying magnetic exponents for weak disorder, and more fixed point solutions under strong disorder, with some exponents independent of N (superuniversality).
AI.motivation: To understand the effects of quenched disorder on the N-color Ashkin-Teller model (N Ising models coupled by four-spin interactions) in two dimensions, particularly the fixed point structure and critical exponents under varying disorder strength.
AI.method: Scale invariant scattering theory applied to derive exact renormalization group fixed point equations for the two-dimensional N-color Ashkin-Teller model with quenched disorder.
AI.result: For weak disorder: a line of fixed points with Ising thermal exponents and continuously varying magnetic exponents for any N>1. For strong disorder: an increased number of fixed point solutions reflecting sensitivity to random coupling distributions. Some critical exponents are independent of N, exhibiting superuniversality.
AI.conclusion: The weak disorder sector preserves Ising-like thermal critical behavior while magnetic exponents vary continuously. Strong disorder enriches the fixed point landscape, and superuniversality (N-independent exponents) emerges as a distinctive feature of random criticality.

title: Thickness-driven crossover from conventional to chiral nonreciprocal superconductivity in kagome metal CsV3Sb5
comment: 19 main pages, 4 main figures, 8 supplementary pages, 5 supplementary figures
summary: Superconductivity and its potential applications are governed by the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter. In the kagome metal CsV3Sb5, most bulk studies indicate conventional s-wave pairing. However, ultrathin flakes exhibit nonreciprocal transport, in particular a zero-field superconducting diode effect, which requires broken inversion and time-reversal symmetries. Here, using thickness dependent transport measurements, we observe the emergence of non-reciprocal second-harmonic magnetotransport signals and a zero-field superconducting diode effect, accompanied by a pronounced reduction of the out-of-plane coherence length with decreasing thickness. Upper critical field measurements further reveal a dimensional crossover from three-dimensional superconductivity in bulk to two-dimensional superconductivity in thin flakes. These findings indicate a thickness-induced chiral superconducting phase that breaks both inversion and time-reversal symmetries in the two-dimensional limit. Our work not only clarifies long-standing controversies regarding the pairing symmetry in CsV3Sb5, but also establishes thin-flake kagome superconductors as a versatile platform for engineering nonreciprocal quantum devices and exploring emergent topological phases.

AI.tldr: Thickness-dependent transport in kagome metal CsV3Sb5 reveals a dimensional crossover from 3D to 2D superconductivity, with emergence of zero-field superconducting diode effect and nonreciprocal signals, indicating a chiral superconducting phase breaking both inversion and time-reversal symmetries in the 2D limit.
AI.motivation: To resolve long-standing controversies about the pairing symmetry in CsV3Sb5 (bulk studies indicate conventional s-wave, but ultrathin flakes show nonreciprocal transport requiring broken inversion and time-reversal symmetries) and to explore the emergence of chiral superconductivity in the 2D limit.
AI.method: Thickness-dependent transport measurements of CsV3Sb5 flakes, including non-reciprocal second-harmonic magnetotransport, zero-field superconducting diode effect measurements, out-of-plane coherence length extraction, and upper critical field analysis to probe dimensional crossover.
AI.result: Observed emergence of non-reciprocal second-harmonic magnetotransport signals and zero-field superconducting diode effect with decreasing thickness, accompanied by pronounced reduction of out-of-plane coherence length; upper critical field measurements revealed a dimensional crossover from 3D to 2D superconductivity.
AI.conclusion: The findings indicate a thickness-induced chiral superconducting phase that breaks both inversion and time-reversal symmetries in the 2D limit. This clarifies pairing symmetry debates in CsV3Sb5 and establishes thin-flake kagome superconductors as a platform for nonreciprocal quantum devices and emergent topological phases.

title: Long-Range Fermi-Polaron Blockade in Monolayer MoSe$_2$
summary: Strong optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level are a central goal for quantum photonics, yet they remain difficult to realize in solid-state systems. In doped two-dimensional semiconductors, coupling between excitons and a degenerate Fermi sea gives rise to exciton-Fermi polarons, many-body quasiparticles whose optical response is governed by fermionic correlations. Here, using femtosecond pump-probe transient absorption microscopy, we directly image the spatially resolved nonlinear optical response of exciton-Fermi polarons in monolayer MoSe$_2$. We observe a pronounced spatial suppression of resonant absorption associated with the attractive Fermi polaron, from which we extract an optical blockade radius that is more than ten times larger than that of the neutral exciton. Microscopic analysis indicates that this extended nonlinearity arises primarily from fermion-mediated interactions between exciton-Fermi polarons. Our results establish exciton-Fermi polarons in two-dimensional semiconductors as electrically tunable, strongly interacting optical quasiparticles, and identify them as a promising platform for ultralow-power nonlinear optical devices.

AI.tldr: Exciton-Fermi polarons in monolayer MoSe₂ exhibit a spatially suppressed resonant absorption with an optical blockade radius over ten times larger than neutral excitons, arising from fermion-mediated interactions, establishing them as electrically tunable, strongly interacting quasiparticles for ultralow-power nonlinear optics.
AI.motivation: Strong optical nonlinearities at the few-photon level are difficult to realize in solid-state systems, and there is a need for electrically tunable, strongly interacting optical quasiparticles for quantum photonics applications.
AI.method: Femtosecond pump-probe transient absorption microscopy was used to directly image the spatially resolved nonlinear optical response of exciton-Fermi polarons in doped monolayer MoSe₂.
AI.result: A pronounced spatial suppression of resonant absorption associated with the attractive Fermi polaron was observed, with an optical blockade radius more than ten times larger than that of the neutral exciton. The extended nonlinearity arises primarily from fermion-mediated interactions between exciton-Fermi polarons.
AI.conclusion: Exciton-Fermi polarons in two-dimensional semiconductors are electrically tunable, strongly interacting optical quasiparticles, offering a promising platform for ultralow-power nonlinear optical devices.

title: Enhanced Loading of a Molecular Magneto-Optical Trap
summary: Molecular magneto-optical traps (MOTs) typically capture orders of magnitude fewer particles than their atomic counterparts due in part to their significantly lower capture velocities. Here, we employ a Stochastic Schrödinger Equation Monte Carlo approach to model a CaF DC MOT to understand the factors limiting capture velocity. We provide physical intuition into the mechanisms that affect capture velocity and identify important parameters and general strategies to improve it. In addition, we point out a loss mechanism intrinsic to molecular MOTs and determine parameter regimes that should be avoided experimentally. We benchmark our simulations against a CaF DC MOT and experimentally implement the improvements predicted by our model. In doing so, we demonstrate a molecular MOT with 1.5 million trapped molecules. This represents an eight-fold improvement and is an important step toward achieving quantum degeneracy with laser cooled molecules.

AI.tldr: The paper uses a Stochastic Schrödinger Equation Monte Carlo approach to model a CaF DC MOT, identifying factors limiting capture velocity and a loss mechanism intrinsic to molecular MOTs. The simulations lead to experimental improvements achieving 1.5 million trapped molecules — an eight-fold improvement over previous molecular MOTs.
AI.motivation: Molecular MOTs capture far fewer particles than atomic MOTs due to significantly lower capture velocities. Understanding and improving capture velocity is critical for advancing toward quantum degeneracy with laser-cooled molecules.
AI.method: Stochastic Schrödinger Equation Monte Carlo approach is employed to model a CaF DC MOT, providing physical intuition into capture velocity limitations and identifying loss mechanisms. Simulations are benchmarked against experiments.
AI.result: Achieved a molecular MOT with 1.5 million trapped molecules, an eight-fold improvement over previous molecular MOTs.
AI.conclusion: The identified parameters and strategies for improving capture velocity, along with avoiding certain parameter regimes, are essential steps toward achieving quantum degeneracy with laser-cooled molecules.

title: Dynamic charges effect on infrared dielectric response of polar materials
summary: Predictive modeling of the infrared dielectric function in polar materials is crucial for thermal management and infrared devices design. While the Green-Kubo molecular dynamics (MD) framework provides a nonperturbative route to compute dielectric responses from dipole fluctuations, yet it commonly relies on the fixed-charge approximation that neglects dynamic charge redistribution during atomic motion. Here, we employ a machine-learning neuroevolution potential with dynamic charges (qNEP) combined with Green-Kubo MD to investigate the dynamic charge effect on the infrared dielectric response of rutile TiO$_2$, a material with large Born effective charges (BEC). Our results show that dynamic charge effects become increasingly important at elevated temperatures and are essential for accurately predicting longitudinal optical phonon features and infrared reflectance. This work establishes that accurate prediction of infrared optical properties in polar materials under thermal excitation requires explicit treatment of dynamic charge evolution.

AI.tldr: The paper uses a machine-learning neuroevolution potential with dynamic charges (qNEP) combined with Green-Kubo MD to show that dynamic charge effects are essential for accurately predicting infrared dielectric properties of polar materials like rutile TiO₂, especially at high temperatures.
AI.motivation: Traditional Green-Kubo MD for dielectric response relies on fixed-charge approximations, neglecting dynamic charge redistribution during atomic motion, which limits accuracy for polar materials with large Born effective charges.
AI.method: A machine-learning neuroevolution potential with dynamic charges (qNEP) is combined with Green-Kubo molecular dynamics to compute infrared dielectric functions from dipole fluctuations in rutile TiO₂.
AI.result: Dynamic charge effects become increasingly important at elevated temperatures and are essential for accurately predicting longitudinal optical phonon features and infrared reflectance.
AI.conclusion: Accurate prediction of infrared optical properties in polar materials under thermal excitation requires explicit treatment of dynamic charge evolution.

title: Strongly-coupled hybrid lattice-plasmons in layered cuprates
summary: Metallic systems with delocalized valence electrons host collective charge density oscillations known as plasmons. On the other hand, conventional insulators do not have free electrons and the low energy charge degrees of freedom are pinned to the ions. The fate of the collective charge excitations in the intermediate regime is an outstanding question. This problem is especially important for strongly correlated systems such as the layered cuprates, where unconventional superconductivity and other emergent phenomena arise from valence electrons on the border between Mott localization and itinerancy. Using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering, we track this evolution in the prototypical electron-doped cuprate Nd2-xCexCuO4. We find a continuous transformation of the low-energy charge response: from an acoustic plasmon in the metallic regime, to a gapped hybrid mode at intermediate doping, and finally to a nearly dispersionless 139 meV excitation at half filling. Remarkably, the 139 meV excitation has approximately twice the energy of the oxygen breathing phonon responsible for the dispersion kink observed in angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, and is consistent with a putative 2-phonon excitation observed in Raman spectroscopy. These results establish a unified picture of collective charge excitations across the phase diagram of electron-doped cuprates, showing that such modes persist across the Mott transition via strong coupling to lattice degrees of freedom and revealing a missing link in the charge dynamics of carrier doped Mott insulators.

AI.tldr: Using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering, this study tracks how collective charge excitations (plasmons) evolve across the metal-insulator transition in electron-doped cuprates Nd2-xCexCuO4, finding a continuous transformation from an acoustic plasmon in the metallic regime to a gapped hybrid mode at intermediate doping, and finally to a ~139 meV excitation at half filling that is consistent with a 2-phonon mode, thus establishing a unified picture of collective charge excitations across the Mott transition via strong coupling to lattice degrees of freedom.
AI.motivation: To understand the fate of collective charge excitations (plasmons) in the intermediate regime between metallic systems (where plasmons exist) and conventional insulators (where charge is pinned to ions), especially in strongly correlated systems like layered cuprates where valence electrons are on the border between Mott localization and itinerancy, and where unconventional superconductivity emerges.
AI.method: Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) was used to track the evolution of low-energy charge response across the phase diagram of the prototypical electron-doped cuprate Nd2-xCexCuO4, covering metallic, intermediate doping, and half-filling regimes.
AI.result: A continuous transformation of the low-energy charge response was observed: an acoustic plasmon in the metallic regime → a gapped hybrid mode at intermediate doping → a nearly dispersionless 139 meV excitation at half filling. The 139 meV excitation has approximately twice the energy of the oxygen breathing phonon responsible for the ARPES dispersion kink, consistent with a putative 2-phonon excitation seen in Raman spectroscopy.
AI.conclusion: These results establish a unified picture of collective charge excitations across the phase diagram of electron-doped cuprates, showing that such modes persist across the Mott transition via strong coupling to lattice degrees of freedom, revealing a missing link in the charge dynamics of carrier-doped Mott insulators.

title: Charged Abelian Higgs phase transitions in three-dimensional compact lattice U(1) gauge models with multicharge scalar matter
summary: We consider three-dimensional (3D) lattice Abelian Higgs models, with compact U(1) gauge variables coupled to a doubly-charged $N$-component complex scalar field (CLAH). We focus on their phase transitions between the disordered-confined (DC) and ordered-deconfined (OD) phases. When they are continuous they belong to the 3D Abelian Higgs (AH) universality class associated with the stable charged fixed point (CFP) of the renormalization-group flow of the 3D AH field theory, or scalar electrodynamics, describing $N$-component complex scalar fields minimally coupled to a U(1) gauge field. This CFP exists only for a sufficiently large number of components, i.e., $N \ge N_d^*$, where the integer $N_d^*$ depends on the spatial dimension $d$ (for example $N_4^*=183$). To estimate $N_3^*$, we look for the minimum number $N_{\rm cL}$ of scalar components of 3D doubly-charged CLAH models developing continuous transitions along their DC-OD transition line. For this purpose, we present finite-size scaling analyses of Monte Carlo simulations for $N\in[4,10]$, up to lattice sizes $L\approx 100$. The results provide evidence of continuous DC-OD transitions for $N=10$, and weak first-order transitions for $N\le 7$. They are not conclusive for $N=8,\,9$. Therefore, we estimate $N_{\rm cL}=9(1)$.

AI.tldr: The paper studies 3D lattice Abelian Higgs models with doubly-charged N-component scalar fields, focusing on phase transitions between disordered-confined and ordered-deconfined phases. Through Monte Carlo simulations for N=4-10 on lattices up to L≈100, they find continuous transitions for N=10 and weak first-order transitions for N≤7, estimating the critical number of components N_cL=9(1) for continuous transitions.
AI.motivation: To estimate N_3^*, the minimum number of scalar components for which the charged fixed point (CFP) exists in 3D Abelian Higgs field theory, by determining the minimum number N_cL of scalar components in doubly-charged CLAH models that develop continuous DC-OD phase transitions.
AI.method: Finite-size scaling analyses of Monte Carlo simulations for doubly-charged CLAH models with N∈[4,10] components on lattice sizes up to L≈100, studying the DC-OD transition line.
AI.result: Continuous DC-OD transitions for N=10, weak first-order transitions for N≤7, inconclusive results for N=8,9. Estimated N_cL=9(1).
AI.conclusion: The minimum number of scalar components for continuous DC-OD transitions in 3D doubly-charged CLAH models is N_cL=9(1), which provides an estimate for N_3^*.

title: Stability Analysis of Superconductivity in $\textit{P6/mmm}$-LaSc$_2$H$_{24}$ and its Experimental Reproducibility from La-Sc Alloys
summary: In this work, we analyze the feasibility of room-temperature superconductivity in the lanthanum-scandium hydride $\textit{P6/mmm}$-LaSc$_2$H$_{24}$. We demonstrate that the electron-phonon coupling calculations performed using the $σ$-broadening of the double $δ$-function at the Fermi surface lead to a very strong dependence of $\textit{T$_c$}(σ)$ on the arbitrary $σ$, whereas the tetrahedral method for the electron-phonon interaction is free from this drawback and leads to $\textit{T$_c$}$ > 300 K at 300 GPa in agreement with previous predictions. By analyzing the stability of the metallic state of LaSc$_2$H$_{24}$ at 250-300 GPa, we show that this compound is at the edge of the stability region ($ξ$ = 0.54), similar to $\textit{fcc}$ LaH$_{10}$ at 140-150 GPa. Experimental attempts to synthesize LaSc$_2$H$_{24}$ at 250-280 GPa starting from the (La,Sc$_2$) alloy are unsuccessful and indicate the absence of even traces of superconductivity at 245-300 K in all the resulting La-Sc-H hydrides. The method for preparing the precursor by simultaneous deposition of La and Sc metals may be a key factor for the successful synthesis of LaSc$_2$H$_{24}$.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes room-temperature superconductivity in LaSc₂H₂₄, showing that using the tetrahedral method (rather than σ-broadening) yields Tc > 300 K at 300 GPa, but experimental synthesis attempts failed to produce this phase or detect superconductivity at 245-300 K.
AI.motivation: To verify the feasibility of room-temperature superconductivity in the predicted hydride LaSc₂H₂₄ and resolve methodological discrepancies in electron-phonon coupling calculations.
AI.method: Compare σ-broadening vs. tetrahedral methods for electron-phonon coupling; analyze metallic stability via ξ parameter; conduct experimental synthesis attempts from (La,Sc₂) alloy at 250-280 GPa.
AI.result: The tetrahedral method gives Tc > 300 K at 300 GPa while σ-broadening yields arbitrary σ-dependent Tc; LaSc₂H₂₄ is at the edge of stability (ξ=0.54) similar to fcc LaH₁₀; experimental synthesis from alloy failed to produce LaSc₂H₂₄ or show superconductivity at 245-300 K.
AI.conclusion: Room-temperature superconductivity in LaSc₂H₂₄ remains theoretically plausible but experimentally unconfirmed; successful synthesis likely requires simultaneous deposition of La and Sc metals rather than using pre-formed alloy.

title: Nanoparticle manipulation with a carbon fiber tip in an electron microscope for $μ$-SQUID magnetometry
comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, suppl-info available through email
summary: We report a carbon-fiber-tip based nanomanipulation system integrated into a scanning electron microscope for individual nanoparticle (NP) manipulation on a surface. Electrochemically etched amorphous carbon fiber tips with excellent mechanical rigidity and sub-100 nm apex radii effectively reduce the van der Waals adhesion and enable reliable positioning of about 100 nm size NPs with about 100 nm precision. This system combines a piezoelectric bimorph for vertical tip motion, a four-quadrant piezo-tube for two-dimensional fine tip control and a two-dimensional piezoelectric walker for coarse lateral translation. Using this setup, we successfully position single Fe$_3$O$_4$ magnetic NPs on micron sized superconducting quantum interference devices for optimal magnetic coupling between them and probe a NP's magnetism.

AI.tldr: A carbon-fiber-tip nanomanipulation system integrated into a scanning electron microscope enables precise (~100 nm precision) positioning of individual ~100 nm nanoparticles on surfaces, demonstrated by placing Fe₃O₄ magnetic NPs onto superconducting quantum interference devices for optimal magnetic coupling and magnetism probing.
AI.motivation: To enable reliable, precise positioning of individual nanoparticles on surfaces for optimal coupling with micro-scale devices (e.g., SQUIDs), overcoming van der Waals adhesion challenges that hinder conventional nanomanipulation.
AI.method: An SEM-integrated nanomanipulation system using electrochemically etched amorphous carbon fiber tips (sub-100 nm apex, high rigidity), combining a piezoelectric bimorph (vertical motion), four-quadrant piezo-tube (fine 2D control), and 2D piezoelectric walker (coarse lateral translation).
AI.result: Successfully positioned single Fe₃O₄ magnetic NPs (~100 nm) on micron-sized SQUIDs with ~100 nm precision, achieving optimal magnetic coupling and enabling probing of individual nanoparticle magnetism.
AI.conclusion: Carbon-fiber-tip nanomanipulation effectively reduces van der Waals adhesion and provides sufficient precision (~100 nm) for placing ~100 nm NPs onto functional micro-devices, enabling single-particle magnetic studies.

title: Synthesizability, hardness, and stacking order in multicomponent transition metal carbides from machine-learned potentials
summary: Multicomponent transition metal carbides are promising for extreme-environment applications, but identifying compositions that are both synthesizable and hard remains challenging. We fine-tune the MACE machine-learned interatomic potential on approximately 28,000 density functional theory calculations spanning the composition space of groups 4-6 transition metals and carbon to predict the thermodynamic stability and elastic properties of multicomponent carbides. The fine-tuned model achieves formation energy errors of ~ 10 meV/atom for thermodynamically relevant structures with only 20% of the training data. We screen over 1500 equiatomic compositions across rocksalt, hexagonal, and hcp prototypes, combining free energy models with elasticity-based hardness surrogates. Synthesizability predictions at 1500°C agree well with experimental reports for both single-phase and multiphase carbides. The group number of the constituent metals governs both stability and hardness. Free energy contributions from short-range order are small, typically a few meV/atom, indicating that a perfectly disordered solid solution provides a reasonable approximation for high-throughput screening. For compositions mixing group 4/5 and group 6 metals, we identify a new family of stacking-ordered phases with formation energies well below those of disordered rocksalt or hexagonal structures. DFT calculations corroborate these predictions and suggest that stacking-ordered phases should be experimentally accessible in multicomponent carbides. This study provides a framework for screening synthesizable multicomponent materials with target properties, identifies promising carbide compositions across the full nine-component space, and reveals a new class of stacking-ordered carbides accessible only in multicomponent compositions.

AI.tldr: Fine-tuning a MACE machine-learned interatomic potential on ~28,000 DFT calculations enables high-throughput screening of over 1500 multicomponent carbide compositions, identifying synthesizable hard phases and discovering a new family of stacking-ordered carbides in compositions mixing group 4/5 and group 6 metals.
AI.motivation: Multicomponent transition metal carbides are promising for extreme-environment applications, but identifying compositions that are both synthesizable and hard remains challenging.
AI.method: Fine-tuned MACE interatomic potential on ~28,000 DFT calculations; screened over 1500 equiatomic compositions across rocksalt, hexagonal, and hcp prototypes using free energy models and elasticity-based hardness surrogates.
AI.result: Formation energy errors of ~10 meV/atom with only 20% training data; synthesizability predictions at 1500°C agree well with experiments; discovered stacking-ordered phases with formation energies below disordered rocksalt or hexagonal structures.
AI.conclusion: Group number governs stability and hardness; short-range order contributions are small; stacking-ordered carbides are experimentally accessible in multicomponent compositions; provides a framework for screening synthesizable multicomponent materials with target properties.

title: Tetrahedrally ferromagnetic correlations and a glassy-freezing anomaly in the breathing pyrochlore magnet $\mathrm{AgInCr_4S_8}$ with partial $A$-site disorder
comment: 14 pages, 6 figures, accepted in Physical Review B
summary: We investigate the chromium breathing pyrochlore sulfide $\mathrm{AgInCr_4S_8}$, a chromium-based thiospinel, by synchrotron x-ray and neutron powder diffraction, dc magnetization, and heat capacity. Diffraction confirms the $F\bar{4}3m$ breathing structure with alternating large and small $\mathrm{Cr_4}$ tetrahedra, a large breathing ratio ($d^\prime/d = 1.106$ at 300 K), and substantial Ag/In intermixing on the $A$ sublattice ($\sim 16\%$). No structural transition or magnetic Bragg peaks are detected down to 1.5 K. An enlarged low-angle difference plot between the 1.5 and 20 K neutron diffraction patterns shows a weak broad diffuse-like enhancement, consistent with short-range or frozen correlated moments within the sensitivity of the present data. Susceptibility yields a positive Weiss temperature $θ_{\mathrm{W}} = +92$ K and a moment enhancement in 30--60 K, while the magnetic entropy released by $\sim 30$ K approaches a scale of order $R\ln 13$, together consistent with the development of short-range tetrahedral ferromagnetic correlations and an effective $S = 6$ cluster-moment picture. A broad susceptibility cusp with ZFC--FC bifurcation and a low-temperature specific heat anomaly near 9 K indicate a phenomenological glassy-freezing anomaly without long-range order. $\mathrm{AgInCr_4S_8}$ provides a benchmark for the interplay of strong breathing distortion and quenched $A$-site disorder in chromium breathing pyrochlores.

AI.tldr: AgInCr4S8, a chromium breathing pyrochlore sulfide, exhibits strong breathing distortion (ratio 1.106), ~16% Ag/In site intermixing, no long-range magnetic order down to 1.5 K, but shows short-range ferromagnetic correlations forming S=6 cluster moments, a glassy freezing anomaly near 9 K, and positive Weiss temperature (+92 K), demonstrating interplay between breathing distortion and A-site disorder.
AI.motivation: To investigate the structural and magnetic properties of AgInCr4S8, a chromium-based breathing pyrochlore sulfide, and understand how strong breathing distortion and quenched A-site disorder collectively suppress long-range order while promoting short-range ferromagnetic correlations and glassy freezing.
AI.method: Synchrotron x-ray and neutron powder diffraction, dc magnetization, and heat capacity measurements were performed on AgInCr4S8, with analysis of structural parameters (breathing ratio, site intermixing), magnetic susceptibility, specific heat, and neutron diffraction difference plots.
AI.result: Confirmed F-43m breathing structure with alternating large/small Cr4 tetrahedra, breathing ratio 1.106 at 300 K, ~16% Ag/In intermixing. No structural transition or magnetic Bragg peaks down to 1.5 K. Weak diffuse scattering enhancement at low angles. Positive Weiss temperature +92 K, magnetic entropy ~Rln13, broad susceptibility cusp with ZFC-FC bifurcation, and specific heat anomaly near 9 K indicating glassy freezing.
AI.conclusion: AgInCr4S8 serves as a benchmark system where strong breathing distortion combined with A-site disorder suppresses long-range magnetic order, instead yielding short-range tetrahedral ferromagnetic correlations (effective S=6 cluster moments) and a phenomenological glassy freezing transition near 9 K.

title: Prototype-Guided Latent Alignment for Data-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Molecular Foundation Models
summary: Machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) have transformed materials discovery by leveraging graph neural networks (GNNs) to predict material properties with near density functional theory (DFT) accuracy. While large-scale pretrained foundation models offer transferable baseline representations, they frequently struggle to generalise to out-of-distribution (OOD) target systems -- a common challenge in modelling complex or chemically diverse materials. Fine-tuning is the standard remedy, but the high cost of generating DFT-labelled configurations confines adaptation to data-scarce regimes, where over-parameterised GNNs amplify overfitting and degrade target-domain performance. To address this, we propose a prototype-based alignment approach for data-efficient fine-tuning of MLIPs. Our method identifies local structural similarities between the source and target domains by grouping atoms with analogous chemical environments based on their latent representations. Each target-domain atom's energy contribution is aligned to its source-domain prototype, introducing an inductive bias that anchors fine-tuned representations to the pretrained structure, encouraging effective reuse of learned interactions and improving generalisation without restrictive assumptions on the target chemistry. We evaluate our method on the rMD17 benchmark using equivariant MACE and invariant SchNet across varying data budgets, and extend evaluation to the MACE-OFF foundation models on the SPICE dataset. Our approach consistently improves predictive accuracy in the low-data regime, reducing energy MAE by up to 18% over standard fine-tuning baselines.

AI.tldr: Proposes a prototype-based alignment method for data-efficient fine-tuning of MLIPs that anchors target-domain representations to source-domain prototypes based on local chemical environment similarity, reducing energy MAE by up to 18% in low-data regimes.
AI.motivation: Large-scale pretrained MLIP foundation models struggle to generalize to out-of-distribution (OOD) target systems, and fine-tuning is hindered by the high cost of DFT-labeled data, leading to overfitting in over-parameterized GNNs under data-scarce conditions.
AI.method: Prototype-based alignment: identifies local structural similarities between source and target domains by grouping atoms with analogous chemical environments via latent representations, then aligns each target-domain atom's energy contribution to its source-domain prototype, introducing an inductive bias that anchors fine-tuned representations to the pretrained structure.
AI.result: Evaluated on rMD17 benchmark (equivariant MACE and invariant SchNet) and SPICE dataset (MACE-OFF foundation models); consistently improves predictive accuracy in low-data regime, reducing energy MAE by up to 18% over standard fine-tuning baselines.
AI.conclusion: The prototype-based alignment approach enables data-efficient fine-tuning of MLIPs by reusing learned interactions from pretrained models without restrictive assumptions on target chemistry, effectively mitigating overfitting in data-scarce scenarios.

title: Entropy of Liquids and Glasses from Recurring Structural Patterns
summary: We compute the low-temperature configurational entropy of a two-dimensional supercooled liquid. Our method, based on a higher-dimensional version of the Grassberger--Procaccia algorithm, can be implemented in a manner that is entirely agnostic with respect to both the dynamics and the theoretical framework, as any genuine notion of order should be. In this construction, entropy is obtained as the decay rate of recurrent structural patterns with increasing patch size, directly linking entropy reduction to the growing persistence of amorphous order. Because the method requires only particle positions, without any knowledge of the interaction potential or even of the particle sizes, it can be applied directly to both equilibrium and nonequilibrium aging configurations. The resulting configurational entropy, together with the higher-order Rényi complexities, agree quantitatively with values obtained from conventional definitions. Remarkably, the entropies measured during aging coincide with their equilibrium counterparts when compared at the same inherent-structure energy.

AI.tldr: A method based on a higher-dimensional Grassberger-Procaccia algorithm computes configurational entropy in 2D supercooled liquids from particle positions alone, without requiring dynamics or interaction potential information, and shows that aging entropies match equilibrium values at the same inherent-structure energy.
AI.motivation: To develop a method for computing configurational entropy in supercooled liquids that is agnostic to dynamics and theoretical framework, relying only on particle positions, and to understand how entropy reduction relates to the growing persistence of amorphous order.
AI.method: A higher-dimensional version of the Grassberger-Procaccia algorithm that measures configurational entropy as the decay rate of recurrent structural patterns with increasing patch size, requiring only particle positions without knowledge of interaction potentials or particle sizes.
AI.result: The method yields configurational entropy and higher-order Rényi complexities that agree quantitatively with conventional definitions. Entropies measured during aging coincide with equilibrium counterparts when compared at the same inherent-structure energy.
AI.conclusion: Configurational entropy can be measured directly from particle positions in a framework-agnostic manner, and aging configurational entropy is determined solely by the inherent-structure energy rather than the thermal history.

title: Electron Doping of $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$ Thin Films: Candidate Metal Dopants and Their Potential Impact on Superconductivity
summary:
The bilayer Ruddlesden-Popper nickelate $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$ has emerged as a promising platform for exploring and understanding high-temperature superconductivities. While most prior doping studies
  have focused on hole doping via strontium (Sr) substitution or by tuning oxygen content, electron doping remains largely unexplored. In this work,we systematically investigate electron doping in $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$ thin films through
  tetravalent element substitution, employing first-principles density functional theory calculations.
  Our results reveal that, unlike in cuprates, $\mathrm{cerium}$ (Ce) doping is difficult to effectively introduce electron carriers into the low-energy bands. In contrast, zirconium (Zr), hafnium (Hf), and thorium (Th) can act as efficient electron dopants. These element substitutions can significantly increase the interlayer hopping $t_{\perp}$ between $d_{z^2}$ orbitals, which may lead to enhanced superexchange coupling $J_{\perp}$ , and thereby potentially elevated superconducting $T_c$. We evaluate the interaction parameters using constrained random phase approximation. Our results identify candidate dopants for achieving electron-doped $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$, offering a route to clarify the ongoing debate on pairing mechanisms in this system.

AI.tldr: This paper uses DFT calculations to study electron doping in La₃Ni₂O₇ thin films via tetravalent element substitution. Ce is ineffective as an electron dopant, while Zr, Hf, and Th are efficient. These substitutions enhance interlayer hopping t⊥ between d_z² orbitals, potentially increasing superexchange coupling J⊥ and superconducting Tc.
AI.motivation: While hole doping in La₃Ni₂O₇ (via Sr or oxygen tuning) has been studied, electron doping remains largely unexplored. This work aims to systematically investigate electron doping via tetravalent element substitution to clarify pairing mechanisms.
AI.method: First-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations and constrained random phase approximation (cRPA) for interaction parameters.
AI.result: Ce doping is ineffective at introducing electron carriers; Zr, Hf, and Th are efficient electron dopants. These substitutions significantly increase interlayer hopping t⊥ between d_z² orbitals, potentially enhancing J⊥ and Tc.
AI.conclusion: Candidate dopants for electron-doped La₃Ni₂O₇ are identified, offering a route to resolve the debate on pairing mechanisms in this system.

title: Alternative origins of polarity in compressively strained SrTiO3-RENiO3 capacitors
summary: Since its original prediction 25 years ago, room-temperature out-of-plane ferroelectricity in compressively strained SrTiO3 remains an ongoing pursuit. In this work, we investigate the structural, electrical and electromechanical properties of highly strained epitaxial SrTiO3 capacitors with rare earth nickelate electrodes. The SrTiO3 layers experience compressive strains up to -3% and exhibit pronounced tetragonality, comparable to that of bulk PbTiO3. Variable-temperature electrical measurements and room-temperature piezoresponse force microscopy reveal butterfly-shaped capacitance-voltage hysteresis and domain-like electromechanical response typical of ferroelectric materials. However, the overall behavior is inconsistent with a stable ferroelectric state. We therefore propose an alternative mechanism for the observed polarity in our samples based on spatially inhomogeneous internal fields. Our first-principles calculations show that such fields may arise from charge discontinuities between the formally charged NdNiO3 layers and charge-neutral SrTiO3 layers.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates strained SrTiO3 capacitors with nickelate electrodes, finding ferroelectric-like behavior that is actually caused by spatially inhomogeneous internal fields from charge discontinuities between layers, not a stable ferroelectric state.
AI.motivation: To experimentally realize and understand the long-predicted room-temperature out-of-plane ferroelectricity in compressively strained SrTiO3, which was predicted 25 years ago but remains unconfirmed.
AI.method: Highly strained epitaxial SrTiO3 capacitors (up to -3% compressive strain) with rare earth nickelate (NdNiO3) electrodes were fabricated and characterized using variable-temperature electrical measurements, room-temperature piezoresponse force microscopy, and first-principles calculations.
AI.result: Despite observing butterfly-shaped capacitance-voltage hysteresis and domain-like electromechanical response typical of ferroelectrics, the overall behavior is inconsistent with a stable ferroelectric state. The observed polarity is instead attributed to spatially inhomogeneous internal fields from charge discontinuities between charged NdNiO3 and charge-neutral SrTiO3 layers.
AI.conclusion: The apparent ferroelectricity in compressively strained SrTiO3 is not a true stable ferroelectric state but arises from inhomogeneous internal fields due to interfacial charge discontinuities, providing an alternative explanation for the observed polarity.

title: Shear Viscosity at the van Hove singularity
summary: The applicability of the semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory is fundamentally challenged in strongly correlated systems where quasiparticle excitations are ill-defined. When the fermion spectral broadening becomes much larger than the boson broadening, the Boltzmann approach to transport is not always valid, particularly in the dirty limit of the critical regime. Using a diagrammatic Kubo formalism, we compute several critical transport coefficients at a van Hove singularity and show that, while the conductivity happens to agree with the Boltzmann result, the dc shear viscosity exhibits qualitatively different behavior. The diagrammatic Kubo results are more reliable because, under the fermion sharp peak approximation--an assumption that strictly breaks down in the dirty critical limit--we demonstrate that the leading order Feynman diagrams reduce to the Boltzmann equation. The same critical model, which can also account for strange metal, makes experimentally testable predictions for the optical and dc shear viscosities, ${\rm Re}[η(Ω)]\sim (|Ω|^{3/2}+T^{3/2})/Ω^2$ and ${\rm Re}[η(Ω=0)]\sim T$, providing further opportunities to assess the validity of our theoretical framework.

AI.tldr: This paper challenges Boltzmann transport theory in strongly correlated systems with ill-defined quasiparticles. Using diagrammatic Kubo formalism at a van Hove singularity, the authors show that conductivity agrees with Boltzmann predictions but dc shear viscosity deviates qualitatively. They derive testable predictions for optical and dc shear viscosities: Re[η(Ω)]∼(|Ω|^(3/2)+T^(3/2))/Ω² and Re[η(Ω=0)]∼T.
AI.motivation: To address the fundamental challenge to semiclassical Boltzmann transport theory in strongly correlated systems where quasiparticle excitations are ill-defined, particularly in the dirty limit of the critical regime when fermion spectral broadening exceeds boson broadening.
AI.method: Diagrammatic Kubo formalism at a van Hove singularity, with systematic comparison to the Boltzmann equation under the fermion sharp peak approximation.
AI.result: Conductivity agrees with Boltzmann predictions, but dc shear viscosity shows qualitatively different behavior. Derived scaling laws: Re[η(Ω)]∼(|Ω|^(3/2)+T^(3/2))/Ω² and Re[η(Ω=0)]∼T, with experimental relevance to strange metal behavior.
AI.conclusion: The diagrammatic Kubo approach is more reliable than Boltzmann theory in the dirty critical limit. The fermion sharp peak approximation is shown to reduce to the Boltzmann equation at leading order and strictly breaks down in the regime of interest, validating the need for the Kubo formalism. Predictions for optical and dc shear viscosities offer experimental tests of the framework.

title: Universal thermokinetic decomposition of short-time information fluctuations
summary: Biological, artificial, and physical systems dissipate energy to accurately transmit information. While tools of information theory have been used to characterize information-processing capabilities, how reliably this information is acquired along individual trajectories, and which aspects require a thermodynamic cost, is an open question. In this work, we focus on the stochastic predictability of an arbitrary Langevin dynamics, defined as the pointwise mutual information between the current and future states of a system. We show that the fluctuations of predictability obey a universal thermokinetic decomposition at short times, which reveals that information fluctuations are suppressed by energy dissipation and become stronger with increased dynamical activity. Remarkably, we find that the average predictability, i.e., the short-time mutual information, does not carry any dependence on the underlying thermodynamic and kinetic features. Thus, the role of dissipation at short times is not to enhance information, but to reduce its fluctuations. Such dissipative control is effective only when instantiated by nonlinear operations. Moreover, energy consumption governs short- and long-time precision in stochastic oscillators through structurally different mechanisms that can be independently tuned. Our decomposition offers a fundamental thermodynamic basis for understanding the reliability of information transmission in nonequilibrium systems, the constraints on precision in biological systems, and the design of energy-limited control strategies.

AI.tldr: This paper reveals that at short times, the predictability (pointwise mutual information) of Langevin dynamics obeys a universal thermokinetic decomposition: average predictability is independent of thermodynamics, while fluctuations are suppressed by dissipation and amplified by dynamical activity. Nonlinear operations are required for dissipative control of fluctuations, and distinct mechanisms govern precision in stochastic oscillators at short and long times.
AI.motivation: To understand how reliably information is acquired along individual trajectories in stochastic systems and which aspects of information processing inherently require a thermodynamic cost.
AI.method: The authors derive a universal thermokinetic decomposition of predictability fluctuations for arbitrary Langevin dynamics at short times, analyzing the relationship between pointwise mutual information, energy dissipation, and dynamical activity.
AI.result: Average predictability is independent of thermodynamic/kinetic features; information fluctuations are suppressed by dissipation and enhanced by dynamical activity; nonlinear operations are necessary for dissipative control; short- and long-time precision in stochastic oscillators are governed by structurally different, independently tunable mechanisms.
AI.conclusion: The role of dissipation at short times is not to enhance average information but to reduce its fluctuations, providing a fundamental thermodynamic basis for reliability in nonequilibrium systems and constraints on precision in biological systems.

title: Disentangling Spin Pumping and Two-Magnon Scattering Contributions to Gilbert Damping in YIG/V Bilayers
summary: In this work, we investigate the magnetic damping and spin pumping response of YIG-based bilayers incorporating vanadium (V) as the normal metal layer via broadband ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) measurements as a function of YIG thickness. We show that the apparent enhancement of the Gilbert damping in YIG/V bilayers cannot be solely attributed to spin pumping. Instead, two-magnon scattering (TMS) plays a dominant role in governing the thickness dependence of the damping in the nanometer regime. By applying a thickness-dependent damping model that accounts for both spin pumping and two-magnon scattering contributions, we successfully disentangle the different relaxation contributions. Our analysis reveals that neglecting two-magnon scattering leads to an overestimation of the spin-pumping contribution and consequently to unphysically large values of the effective spin-mixing conductance. After isolating the intrinsic spin pumping contribution, we extract a thickness-independent effective spin-mixing conductance of $g^{\uparrow\downarrow}_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1.33 \times 10^{18}~\mathrm{m^{-2}}$. These findings provide a more accurate framework for quantifying spin transport parameters in FM/HM systems and emphasize the necessity of accounting for extrinsic damping mechanisms when interpreting spin pumping and inverse spin Hall effect experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates magnetic damping in YIG/V bilayers and shows that two-magnon scattering (TMS), not just spin pumping, dominates the thickness-dependent damping enhancement. By disentangling these contributions, they extract an accurate, thickness-independent effective spin-mixing conductance of $g^{\uparrow\downarrow}_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1.33 \times 10^{18}~\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, demonstrating that neglecting TMS leads to overestimation of spin-pumping parameters.
AI.motivation: To accurately quantify spin transport parameters in YIG/V bilayers by distinguishing between intrinsic spin pumping and extrinsic two-magnon scattering contributions to magnetic damping, which is often conflated in previous studies.
AI.method: Broadband ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) measurements on YIG/V bilayers as a function of YIG thickness, combined with a thickness-dependent damping model that accounts for both spin pumping and two-magnon scattering contributions.
AI.result: Two-magnon scattering dominates the thickness-dependent damping in nanometer-thick YIG/V bilayers; neglecting TMS leads to overestimation of spin pumping and unphysically large effective spin-mixing conductance; after isolating intrinsic spin pumping, a thickness-independent $g^{\uparrow\downarrow}_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1.33 \times 10^{18}~\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ is obtained.
AI.conclusion: Extrinsic damping mechanisms, particularly two-magnon scattering, must be accounted for when interpreting spin pumping and inverse spin Hall effect experiments in ferromagnet/heavy-metal systems to avoid overestimating spin transport parameters.

title: Finite-temperature micromagnetic model bridging atomic- and macro-scale magnetism
summary: A multi-scale finite-temperature micromagnetic model is presented, based on the Landau-Lifshitz equation and the Bernoulli differential equation. This model accurately reproduces classic Maxwell magnetostatics of paramagnets for high temperatures and accurately reproduces standard micromagnetics described by the conventional Landau-Lifshitz model in ferromagnets.
